sentences.text:
Order 
This Miscellaneous Appeal has been filed under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 by the appellant, who claims to be the owner of the offending vehicle.

The appeal is directed against the award dated 20.09.2005 passed by the Fourth Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Fast Track), Shivpuri (M.P.), in Claim Case No. 72/2005 (hereinafter referred to as "the Claims Tribunal").
2.

entities.text: Fourth Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Fast Track), Shivpuri
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The date of the accident and the finding recorded by the Claims Tribunal regarding negligence are not in dispute.
The appellant has preferred the present appeal seeking exoneration from liability to pay the compensation awarded by the Claims Tribunal.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that at the time of the accident, the appellant had already sold the offending vehicle and, therefore, he cannot be held liable to pay compensation to the claimant.
On this basis, a prayer was made for absolving the appellant from liability.
4. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent supported the impugned award and prayed for dismissal of the appeal.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4716 2 MA-4-2006 5.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the Claims Tribunal.

sentences.text:
Owner is defined under Section 2(30) of the Motor Vehicle Act as a person in whose name a motor vehicle stands registered and where such person is a minor, the guardian of such minor, and in relation to a motor vehicle which is the subject of a hire-purchase, agreement, or an agreement of lease or an agreement of hypothecation, the person in possession of the vehicle under that agreement;
7.
In the present case, it is an admitted fact that at the time of the accident, the appellant was the registered owner of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, he is liable to pay compensation to the claimant.
Mere assertion that the vehicle had been sold, without transfer of registration in accordance with law, does not absolve the registered owner from liability.
8. In view of the above discussion, no interference is warranted in the impugned award passed by the Claims Tribunal.
9. Accordingly, the Miscellaneous Appeal is dismissed.
No order as to costs.
